subtitle: In Vallabhi’s quiet streets, a Shaiva king guards many paths to wisdom.

panels.shot: epic mid-shot, low angle, king on palace terrace overlooking Vallabhi
panels.action: Siladitya I Dharmaditya stands in royal ornaments with a Shaiva mark on his brow, gazing over the bustling university city of Vallabhi with monasteries and temples dotting the horizon.

dialogue.text: Centuries after he died, Xuanzang’s hosts still praised Siladitya of Vallabhi—how did a Shaiva king earn such lasting memory in a city of many faiths?

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद भी शुआनज़ांग के मेज़बान वल्लभी के शीलादित्य को याद करते रहे—कई मज़हबों के शहर में इस शैव राजा की याद इतनी लंबी कैसे चली?

panels.shot: wide aerial shot over Saurashtra coast
panels.action: A sweeping view of western India in the early 7th century shows ports along the coast, trade ships on the sea, and inland routes leading toward the walled city of Vallabhi.

dialogue.text: Around 600 CE, western India was a crossroads of sea trade, old Gupta loyalties and rising local powers. Vallabhi, capital of the Maitrakas, watched all roads and ships.

i18n.hi: लगभग 600 ईस्वी में पश्चिम भारत समुंदर व्यापार, पुराने गुप्त संबंधों और नई स्थानीय ताकतों का चौराहा था। मैत्रक राजधानी वल्लभी से सड़कों और जहाज़ों पर नज़र रहती थी।

panels.action: Inside a stone-pillared hall, Siladitya I Dharmaditya sits on a modest throne, attendants and scribes nearby, as a priest traces a trident emblem on a banner behind him.

dialogue.text: Siladitya I, called Dharmaditya in his grants, ruled the Maitrakas when Gupta authority had faded. His court wore Shaiva marks, but his realm carried many voices.

i18n.hi: शीलादित्य प्रथम, जो अपने फरमानों में धर्मादित्य कहलाते थे, गुप्त सत्ता ढीली पड़ने पर मैत्रकों के राजा बने। दरबार पर शैव रंग था, पर राज्य में कई आवाज़ें थीं।

panels.shot: close-up on Siladitya examining a copper-plate
panels.action: Siladitya leans forward on his throne, studying a freshly engraved copper plate held by a royal scribe, the plate glinting with tiny lines of script.

dialogue.text: Our window into his reign is not a poet’s praise but copper-plate grants—dry lines of land, rights and names that show what this Shaiva king chose to protect.

i18n.hi: उनके राज का सच कवि की प्रशंसा नहीं, बल्कि ताम्रपत्रों में दिखता है—ज़मीन, हक़ और नामों की सीधी लकीरें, जो बताती हैं कि इस शैव राजा ने क्या बचाए रखा।

panels.shot: detail shot of copper plate on low table
panels.action: A copper plate rests on a low wooden stand; engraved around a central seal are lines recording a land grant, while Siladitya’s hand is seen pointing to a key phrase.

dialogue.text: Some plates grant villages and revenues to Brahmanas and temples. Others name monasteries and scholars of Buddhist and Jain paths, bound into the same official script.

i18n.hi: कुछ ताम्रपत्र ब्राह्मणों और मंदिरों को गाँव और लगान सौंपते हैं। कुछ में बौद्ध और जैन विहारों व विद्वानों के नाम हैं, वही सरकारी लिपि में साथ-साथ दर्ज।

panels.shot: slow push-in mid-shot in audience chamber
panels.action: Monks with simple robes, Jain ascetics with cloth-covered mouths, and Brahmanas with sacred threads stand respectfully before Siladitya as he hears a petition.

dialogue.text: Vallabhi’s fame for learning grew under the Maitrakas. In petitions, different teachers sought royal support, and under Siladitya, their paths met in one audience hall.

i18n.hi: मैत्रकों के समय में वल्लभी की विद्या की शोहरत बढ़ी। दरबार में अलग-अलग आचार्य राजसहायता माँगते, और शीलादित्य के राज में उनकी राहें एक ही सभा में मिलती थीं।

panels.shot: medium shot, king in quiet side-chamber
panels.action: In a quieter chamber, Siladitya sits with advisors around a map, weighing the boundaries of estates and noting monasteries and shrines marked on palm-leaf documents.

dialogue.text: His grants do not declare a modern policy of tolerance. They show a ruler managing land and loyalty, yet choosing to include houses of study among those he endowed.

i18n.hi: उनके फरमान आज की ‘सहिष्णुता नीति’ नहीं बोलते। वे दिखाते हैं कि राजा ज़मीन और निष्ठा सँभालता है, पर अपनी दान-सूची में पाठशालाओं के घर भी जोड़ता है।

panels.shot: wide shot of Vallabhi’s scholarly quarter
panels.action: Rows of brick and wooden buildings form a university quarter: monks discuss in courtyards, students copy manuscripts, and a Jain teacher lectures under a tree.

dialogue.text: By the time Xuanzang reached Vallabhi, decades later, the city held hundreds of Buddhist monks and thriving schools. They spoke highly of an earlier king named Siladitya.

i18n.hi: जब तक शुआनज़ांग वल्लभी पहुँचे, कुछ दशक बीत चुके थे। शहर में सैकड़ों बौद्ध भिक्षु और चहल-पहल वाले विद्यालय थे, जो एक पुराने राजा शीलादित्य की खूबियाँ गिनते थे।

panels.shot: close-up of a monk talking to unseen visitor
panels.action: An elderly monk faces slightly off-frame, gesturing toward distant city walls as if recalling the reign of a past king to a foreign listener.

dialogue.text: Xuanzang’s record, written in China, repeats that local memory: Siladitya of Vallabhi, they said, had been able and compassionate. He ruled long before Xuanzang arrived.

i18n.hi: चीन में लिखी शुआनज़ांग की यात्रा-वृत्त स्थानीय याद दोहराती है: वल्लभी के शीलादित्य, वे कहते, समर्थ और दयालु थे। वे शुआनज़ांग से बहुत पहले राज कर चुके थे।

panels.shot: low-angle mid-shot of Siladitya in temple courtyard
panels.action: Siladitya stands in a Shaiva temple courtyard, a lingam shrine behind him, as a messenger approaches with a scroll bearing a request from a monastery.

dialogue.speaker: siladitya_i_dharmaditya
dialogue.text: A kingdom is not weakened when it feeds minds.

i18n.hi: जो राज्य दिमागों को खिलाता है, वो कमज़ोर नहीं होता।

panels.shot: wide shot of grant ceremony outdoors
panels.action: Under an awning in the palace compound, Siladitya ceremonially hands a rolled copper plate to a group of scholars, while villagers look on from behind a rope barrier.

dialogue.text: His charter language is formal, speaking of meritorious gift, dharma and reward. Yet its impact was practical: fields, taxes, and secure roofs for those keeping texts alive.

i18n.hi: उनके फरमान की भाषा भारी है—पुण्य दान, धर्म और फल की बातें। असर मगर ठोस था: खेत, कर और सुरक्षित छतें उन लोगों के लिए जो ग्रंथों को ज़िंदा रखते थे।

panels.shot: medium shot in royal court with military retinue visible
panels.action: Siladitya sits in court with armored retainers on one side and a learned Brahmana on the other, scrolls laid out between them, showing the balance between force and law.

dialogue.text: Like any king, Siladitya relied on arms and alliances. What sets him apart in the record is how often his name appears where land is secured for learning and ritual.

i18n.hi: हर राजा की तरह शीलादित्य भी सेना और संधियों पर टिके थे। फर्क रिकॉर्ड में वहाँ दिखता है जहाँ ज़मीन सीख और अनुष्ठान के लिए सुरक्षित होती है—वहाँ उनका नाम बार-बार आता है।

panels.shot: montage wide shot fading from inscription to landscape
panels.action: An engraved copper plate lies half-buried in soil; above it the scene fades into fields, monasteries and temples lit by evening sun across the Maitraka countryside.

dialogue.text: We do not see every decision he made. We see enough to trace a pattern—religious institutions woven into administration, and a king’s name tied to their survival.

i18n.hi: हम उनकी हर सियासी चाल नहीं देख पाते। इतना ज़रूर दिखता है कि धार्मिक संस्थाएँ प्रशासन में बुनी थीं, और उनकी रियासत के टिके रहने में राजा का नाम भी बुना था।

panels.shot: interior shot of scribe copying old charter
panels.action: Generations later, a younger scribe in Vallabhi copies an earlier charter of Siladitya onto fresh leaves, preserving its terms for a new age.

dialogue.text: After Siladitya’s time, Maitraka rulers still cited his grants, his titles, his model. Memory of his fairness traveled not through legend alone, but through copied contracts.

i18n.hi: शीलादित्य के बाद भी मैत्रक शासक उनके फरमानों, उपाधियों और मिसाल का ज़िक्र करते रहे। उनकी न्यायप्रियता की याद सिर्फ़ दंतकथाओं से नहीं, नकल किए गए करारों से चली।

panels.shot: medium shot of Xuanzang writing by lamplight
panels.action: Xuanzang sits in his quarters with a simple lamp, brush in hand, writing about Vallabhi on long paper strips, his face thoughtful as he recalls what monks told him.

dialogue.text: In Chang’an, Xuanzang wrote of Vallabhi’s learning and of Siladitya with respect. His praise is not an eyewitness report, but a record of how a region remembered its king.

i18n.hi: चांग’आन में बैठकर शुआनज़ांग ने वल्लभी की विद्या और शीलादित्य का वर्णन सम्मान से किया। यह आँखों देखा हाल नहीं, बल्कि उस क्षेत्र की स्मृति है कि उसने अपने राजा को कैसे याद रखा।

panels.shot: slow pull-back from close-up to wide, king overlooking city at dusk
panels.action: At dusk, Siladitya stands again on the palace terrace, the city’s temples and monasteries glowing softly, the sea beyond catching the last light.

dialogue.text: In Siladitya’s Vallabhi, Shaiva worship, Buddhist recitation and Jain teaching shared streets. His rule did not erase difference; it kept space for study within power.

i18n.hi: शीलादित्य के वल्लभी में शैव पूजा, बौद्ध पाठ और जैन उपदेश एक ही गलियों में चलते थे। उनकी हुकूमत ने फर्क नहीं मिटाया, बस ताकत के भीतर पढ़ने-सिखने की जगह बचाए रखी।

panels.shot: distant long shot of Vallabhi ruins under open sky
panels.action: Centuries later, the ruined outlines of Vallabhi’s walls and foundations lie under an open sky, while an imagined overlay of copper-plate text shimmers faintly above them.

dialogue.text: Vallabhi’s buildings fell, but charters, chronicles and travelogues still speak his name. Siladitya’s story reminds us that power is most honored when it shelters the life of learning.

i18n.hi: वल्लभी की इमारतें मिट गईं, मगर फरमान, इतिहास और यात्राएँ अभी भी उनका नाम बोलते हैं। शीलादित्य की कहानी याद दिलाती है कि सत्ता सबसे ज़्यादा सम्मानित तब होती है जब वह सीखने की ज़िंदगी को आसरा देती है।

subtitle_i18n.en: In Vallabhi’s quiet streets, a Shaiva king guards many paths to wisdom.
subtitle_i18n.hi: वल्लभी की शांत गलियों में, एक शैव राजा ज्ञान की कई राहों की रखवाली करता है।
